propositions: When an LLM call raises an exception, control leaves PydanticAIRunner.run() without reaching usage_log.record(), so no usage row is written despite potential token burn.
Failed calls write nothing to REBAR_USAGE_LOG, causing spend totals folded from the JSONL to under-report actual spend and making per-step attribution incomplete.
A failed row must be written carrying identifying fields (op, step, model_class, model, provider) plus known token counters, distinguishable from successful calls via an explicit outcome marker.
The failure row must be recorded before interpret_failure() re-raises, within the runner's own except block, without converting or swallowing the original provider exception.
Failed and successful rows must be mutually exclusive within one run() call, and retried calls must not double-count burned budget as delivered work.
